positions.name: GateAsRatifiedRule
positions.frame: How does positional authority instantiate the gate — through directive, formal requirement, scope, and ownership — as a settled rule rather than an argued proposal?
positions.why: Across register (formal directive vs. terse spec-line), style (stock directive phrasing vs. bolded-tag-colon-value fragments), and power/relational reads (legitimate authority, authority-ranking) these four expressions all perform the gate into existence as a ratified operational rule rather than arguing for it: src-1 issues the mandate, src-3 restates it as a spec-line requirement, src-4 fixes its jurisdictional reach, and src-5 assigns accountability. There is a mild tension held here — src-1 and src-3 assert the same requirement twice, once in prose and once in compressed spec form — but the frame reads both as instances of the same authority-move, not a contradiction. src-2 is deliberately excluded: its plain-spoken, evidence-based rationale (informational/rational-persuasion, causal framing) argues FOR the gate rather than performing it, a different directional read.
